description: A 29-year veteran female detective in the Los Angeles Police Department's Robbery-Homicide Division filed a whistleblower lawsuit in Los Angeles County Superior Court in 2024 alleging gender-based harassment, a hostile work environment, and retaliation. According to the complaint, a male supervising detective compared female detectives to sex workers on Figueroa Street, and women in the unit faced ongoing verbal abuse. The suit alleges that after the plaintiff and another female detective complained to the Board of Police Commissioners in September 2023, she was demoted, transferred to an auto theft unit with an 18 percent pay cut, subjected to internal investigations she describes as fabricated, and had her keycard access revoked. The suit names senior LAPD officials including Deputy Chief Marc Reina and Captains Scot Williams and Robin Petillo. After a Los Angeles Times inquiry, the plaintiff was restored to her prior detective rank in July 2024. The city has denied the allegations.
inclusion_concern: Claims center on gender-based hostile work environment, sexist remarks and retaliation rather than sexual assault or physical sexual harassment; confirm this meets the database's threshold for sexual-harassment-centered litigation.
